Reason: write f = sum c_{d,k} a^d z^k (finite support, unique representation). Read as a Laurent polynomial in a over ZZ[z^{+-1}], its a^d-coefficient is c_d(z) = sum_k c_{d,k} z^k, and c_d != 0 in ZZ[z^{+-1}] iff exists k with c_{d,k} != 0 iff exists k with coeffAt d k f != 0 (coeffAt d k f := f.coeff (d,k), LinkLaurentRing.lean:286; AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff of single is Finsupp.single). Hence the printed "largest a-exponent with nonzero coefficient" is max{d : exists k, coeffAt d k f != 0}, which is exactly what the Lean degA clause (statement lines 36-39) asserts: degAZ f is attained (exists k, coeffAt (degAZ f) k f != 0), bounds every exponent with nonzero coefficient (forall d k, coeffAt d k f != 0 -> d <= degAZ f), and is the unique such integer. Symmetrically for mindegA (lines 42-45) and for the z-subscript degZ/mindegZ (lines 47-55), where the source already works in ZZ[a^{+-1},z^{+-1}] directly. The alternative reading of "coefficient" as the ZZ-coefficient of a^d z^k gives the same set {d : exists k, c_{d,k} != 0}, so both readings agree. Under the hood, Link.degA f = f.supDegree wtA = f.coeff.support.sup (fun e => (e.1 : WithBot ZZ)) (Mathlib: abbrev supDegree f := f.coeff.support.sup D); WithBot ZZ is linearly ordered so sup = max; degAZ f = (degA f).unbotD 0 and unbotD_coe : unbotD d (x : WithBot) = x, so for f != 0 (support nonempty, degA f != bot) degAZ f is the max first coordinate of the support. infDegree/untopD are the dual. Concrete checks: f = a^2 z^{-1} + a^2 z^3 - 1 has c_2 = z^{-1}+z^3, c_0 = -1, printed (deg_a, mindeg_a, deg_z, mindeg_z) = (2,0,3,-1); Lean support {(2,-1),(2,3),(0,0)} gives (2,0,3,-1). f = 5 a^{-3} z^4 - 7 z^{-2} gives (-3,0,4,-2) both ways. "Both are integers" is rendered by degAZ f : ZZ together with Link.degA f = (degAZ f : WithBot ZZ) (so not bot). "Nonzero" is the guard f != 0 on all four degree clauses; no clause says anything at f = 0 (the degAZ 0 = 0 convention of LinkLaurentRing.lean:446 is not in the bundle; domain/monomial/coeff mention no degree). The identification of (ZZ[z^{+-1}])[a^{+-1}] with R = AddMonoidAlgebra ZZ (ZZ x ZZ) is the standard ring isomorphism and the a-exponent of c a^d z^k is d on both sides, so the design reading is faithful for this definition. The monomial clause (line 28: single (d,k) 1 = aUnit^d * zUnit^k; true by monoUnit_zpow/monoUnit_mul) and the coeff clause (lines 31-33: Kronecker value on monomials, extensionality) are notation glue fixing what "a-exponent", "z-exponent" and "coefficient (zero if that monomial is absent)" denote; they add no content beyond that. Points where the Lean is STRONGER than or differs cosmetically from the source, none of which changes the defined objects and none of which I judge a refuting discrepancy: (1) domain : IsDomain R (line 26) asserts the whole ring ZZ[a^{+-1},z^{+-1}] is a domain, while the source says "coefficients in the integral domain ZZ[z^{+-1}]" (a property of the coefficient subring); the Lean clause implies the printed one (nontrivial subring of a domain is a domain) and is a true Mathlib instance (IsDomain R[A] from IsDomain ZZ, IsCancelAdd ZZ, UniqueSums (ZZ x ZZ)), but it is not literally the printed statement.
